land.text: the Albanian lands that had left Serbian rule: Karl Thopia's central Albania (Lord of Kruje), the Muzaka at Berat, the Zenebishi at Gjirokaster, the Shpata at Arta, the Gropa at Ohrid and Debar

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's row also holds Thomas Preljubovic's Ioannina region and, in North Macedonia, land that the Prince Marko page (Prince Marko) assigns to Marko's lordship at Prilep. The Serbian Empire dossier records the secession of Albania by 1371.

land.text: the Albanian lordships taken by the Ottomans: Thopia's Albania (to 1415), Berat (1417), Gjirokaster (1418)

successors.note: The Dukagjini, Kastrioti and Zaharia lordships continue as Ottoman vassals to the League of Lezhe (1444) and have no Cliopatria row after 1421.

capitals.name: Kruje (Kruja)
capitals.note: Composite state with no common capital. Karl Thopia, the leading prince, is 'Lord of Kruje' (infobox) and Kruja was the capital of the earlier Arbanon (the Albanian principalities page); the Dukagjini centre was Lezhe until 1393 (the Albanian principalities page).

keyframe_review.note: 69,530 km2 (62,238 km2 in the gazetteer's cells): Albania 18,000, North Macedonia 22,000 and Greece 12,650 km2, i.e. the Albanian lordships (Thopia, Muzaka, Zenebishi, Shpata, Gropa) together with Thomas Preljubovic's Ioannina region (43 cells, the same cells as Cliopatria's Despotate of Epirus from 1385) and land around Prilep and Bitola (Skopje went to Vuk Brankovic by 1377) that the Prince Marko page gives to Marko's lordship (Prilep, 1371-1395, bounded by the Sar mountains and Skopje, the Vardar and Crna Reka, Ohrid). The page's lead: the principalities 'covered modern day Albania, western and central Kosovo, Epirus, areas up to Corinth'. Marko's lordship needs its own dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers); no infobox area exists on either page. Kept as drawn.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1385-1391 only; from 1392 the shape loses Durrës (new keyframe 1392)

keyframe_review.note: 58,211 km2: the 43 Ioannina-Gjirokaster-Arta cells (10,879 km2) pass to the Despotate of Epirus, 5 cells are added around 19.5-23.4 E, 41.2-42.1 N. Cliopatria dates the loss 1385 (ledger, confidence 1); the Albanian principalities page nevertheless lists a Gjirokaster principality of the Zenebishi for 1373-1418 and an Arta principality of the Shpata for 1355-1416, so the Epirus transfer is Cliopatria's, not the page's. Years only. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1385..1391 from this entry's own 'valid 1385-1391 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

minus.text: Durres and its coast, which Venice holds from 1392

correction.text: the 1385 shape without Durres: Venice 'annexed' it in 1392

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Albanian principalities page has Durres annexed by Venice in 1392 (the Karl Thopia page: Gjergj Thopia 'left Durres to Venice just before he died in 1392'); Cliopatria shows the five-cell loss at 19.5-19.7 E, 41.2-41.6 N only in 1402.

correction.text: the 1395 shape without Durres (Venetian since 1392), valid 1395-1401

keyframe_review.note: 13,518 km2, Albania only, 49 of 50 cells between 19.4 and 20.5 E, 40.3 and 42.0 N. The 158-cell drop (39,974 km2, 19.8-23.4 E, 39.6-43.1 N) is the Ottoman annexation of the Gropa lands (the Albanian principalities page: 'the family ruled until 1395, when it fell to the Ottomans') and of Prince Marko's lordship after the battle of Rovine on 17 May 1395 (the Prince Marko page). Valona and Kanina, separate in Cliopatria, are not in the shape.

12,249 km2: the five Durres cells are gone, matching the 1392 Venetian annexation (the Albanian principalities page, the Karl Thopia page). Thopia's principality is dated 1359-1415 and the Zenebishi's Gjirokaster 1373-1418 (outside the shape); no other change is dated on the pages opened.

12,249 km2, unchanged to 1421. The pages date the Thopia principality to 1415 and Berat to 1417 (ledger) but the shape does not change; the Dukagjini (1387-1444), Kastrioti (1389-1444) and Zaharia (Dagnum 1396-1430) lordships remain in the north. unverified: page budget for the 1415-1421 geometry.

region.text: Albania, 'western and central Kosovo, Epirus' as the lead lists the area; here the Cliopatria row

ledger.note: 1375: the Albanian principalities stand independent. Cliopatria starts the row in 1375; the page has the principalities 'became stronger' in the second half of the 14th century and lists Thopia (1359), Valona (1346-1355), Arta (1355), Gjirokaster (1373) and others, and Karl Thopia was named 'Grande Conte d'Albania' by Gregory XI in 1374 (the Karl Thopia page). No page dates a collective foundation.
1376: Karl Thopia loses Durres. 'He lost Durres in 1376 to Louis of Durazzo.'
1383: Karl Thopia recovers Durres 'after the Navarrese Company left Greece'.

By 1385: the Balsic take Durres. 'By 1383 or 1385, Balsa II had conquered Durres, presumably from Karl Thopia'; Karl Thopia page: Balsa II 'started an offensive' in 1385 and took Durres 'the following year' (the pages conflict; the year is a bridge).

region.text: the Ioannina region and the south of the row: 43 cells

ledger.note: 1385: the Ioannina-Gjirokaster-Arta cells leave the row. Cliopatria moves 43 cells (10,879 km2, 20.0-21.6 E, 39.3-40.3 N) to the Despotate of Epirus in 1385; the page is silent (it lists a Gjirokaster principality of the Zenebishi for 1373-1418 and Arta under the Shpata to 1416), so this records Cliopatria's change.

18 September 1385: Karl Thopia recovers Durres after Savra. Balsa II was killed at Savra 'on 18 September 1385'; 'Thopia recaptured Durres immediately after the battle, probably under Ottoman suzerainty'. The Ottomans took Kruje, Berat and Ulcinj but 'soon withdrew from them'.
1392: Venice annexes Durres. 'Durres was annexed by the Republic of Venice' in 1392 (the Karl Thopia page: Gjergj Thopia 'left Durres to Venice just before he died in 1392').

region.text: the region between Pogradec, Ohrid and Debar

ledger.note: 1395: the Gropa lands fall to the Ottomans. The Gropa 'controlled the region between Pogradec, Ohrid and Debar' and 'ruled until 1395, when it fell to the Ottomans'.

region.text: everything the row loses in 1395: North Macedonia and the Greek border land east of the Albanian highlands

ledger.note: 17 May 1395: Marko's lands and the rest of the east pass to the Ottomans. 'The Battle of Rovine, on 17 May 1395, was won by the Wallachians; Marko and Dragas were killed'; afterwards the Ottomans annexed the lands, forming a province centred in Kyustendil (the page does not date the annexation). Region: the 158 cells Cliopatria drops in 1395.

region.text: Berat and the Myzeqe plain, the Muzaka lands

ledger.note: 1417: Berat falls to the Ottomans. The Muzaka principality of Berat, a despotate since 1335, 'fell under the Ottoman Empire' in 1417 (the page's sentence is garbled; Valona, a separate Cliopatria state, is dated 'until conquered by the Ottoman Turks in 1417'). Thopia's Albania ends in 1415 and Gjirokaster is abolished in 1418 (outside the shape).

region.text: the Albanian lordships still holding in 1421 (Dukagjini, Kastrioti, Zaharia at Dagnum)

ledger.note: 1421: the row ends. No page dates the end of the Albanian principalities as a group; Cliopatria stops in 1421. The page has them continue, as the Dukagjini and Kastrioti lordships, to the League of Lezhe (1444-1480) and as Ottoman vassals.

wars.name: Thopia-Balsic war for Durres

zones.text: Durres and Kruje, the central Albanian coast

wars.outcome: Balsa II and Karl Thopia 'had been fighting for the control of the region' since 1363; Durres changed hands in 1376, 1383 and 1385; Balsa II was killed at Savra in September 1385.
wars.note: The page dates Balsa II's offensive to 1385 and the capture of Durres to 'the following year'; Battle of Savra page: 'By 1383 or 1385'.

wars.name: Battle of Savra (Ottoman campaign in Albania)
wars.outcome: On 18 September 1385 the Ottomans (Hayreddin Pasha, called in by Karl Thopia) defeated and killed Balsa II near Berat/Lushnje; they took Kruje, Berat and Ulcinj but soon withdrew; most local Serbian and Albanian lords became Ottoman vassals.

wars.name: Battle of Rovine (Ottoman annexation of Prince Marko's lands)

zones.text: the land the row loses in 1395

wars.outcome: Marko and Dragas were killed fighting as Ottoman vassals on 17 May 1395 against the Wallachians; the Ottomans annexed their lands afterwards (undated).

certainty.note: Composite of lordships: no treaty line is given on any page opened; frontiers are drawn from the principalities' seats and Cliopatria.

sources.title: Albanian principalities
sources.note: The list of principalities with dates (Thopia 1359-1415, Valona 1346-1417, Arta 1355-1416, Gjirokaster 1373-1418, Dukagjini 1387, Kastrioti 1389, Gropa to 1395), Durres 1392.

sources.title: Battle of Savra
sources.note: 18 September 1385, death of Balsa II, Ottoman gains and withdrawal, Durres.

sources.title: Prince Marko
sources.note: Marko's Prilep lordship 1371-1395, Gropa at Ohrid, Rovine 17 May 1395, Ottoman annexation.

notes: Pages: four of five allowed (Albanian principalities, Karl Thopia, Battle of Savra, Prince Marko). Cliopatria row is a composite, not one state: 1375-1384 it holds the Albanian lordships plus Thomas Preljubovic's Ioannina region (Cliopatria gives the same 43 cells to the Despotate of Epirus from 1385) and Prince Marko's Prilep lordship in North Macedonia; 1395 onward it is central Albania only. Type 'state' kept because the renderer draws territory; the League of Lezhe (1444-1480) is the association and is outside the row. Start 1375 is Cliopatria's (no page dates a collective foundation; the Serbian Empire dossier records the secession by 1371) and end 1421 is Cliopatria's: the pages date Thopia to 1415, Valona to 1417, Berat to 1417 and Gjirokaster to 1418, and Dukagjini, Kastrioti and Zaharia run on. Verdict choices: the 1385 and 1395 shapes are corrected for the Venetian annexation of Durres in 1392 (Cliopatria shows it from 1402). Pages silent on: the 1385 Epirus transfer, the 1375 geometry beyond the list, Thopia's end in 1415 (who ended it), who ruled the Ohrid-Debar land after 1395. Counterparts: serbian-despots (Balsic, the Durres swings), despotate-of-epirus (1385), republic-of-venice (Durres 1392; its dossier records the gain from this row), ottoman-empire (1395, 1417), principality-of-valona-and-kanina (separate Cliopatria row, not in this shape). The ottoman-empire dossier should carry the vassal events for the Albanian lords after Savra (1385) that the page only summarises ('Most local Serbian and Albanian lords became Ottoman vassals'). States needing dossiers: Prince Marko's lordship (Prilep, 1371-1395); Thopia's Principality of Albania (1359-1415); Dukagjini (1387-1444/1479); Kastrioti (1389-1444); Gjirokaster of the Zenebishi (1373-1418); Gropa; Zaharia (Dagnum 1396-1430).
